item.title: España: dos muertos y un desaparecido tras récord de lluvias en Cataluña
item.description: Por primera vez en 143 años, desde que hay estadísticas, Barcelona reporta más de 200 litros de lluvia por metro cuadrado tras una jornada que "pasará a la historia de los registros climáticos", según el Servicio Meteorológico de Cataluña. Casas inundadas, vehículos sumergidos y hospitales afectados conforman la estampa con la que se despertaron varios municipios de la región. El temporal obliga a la cancelación de decenas de vuelos y afecta la circulación en la mayoría de las líneas ferroviarias. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Inka scattered sacred coca leaves over sacrificed llamas, excavation suggests
item.description: Deep in Peru's Acarí Valley lie the ruins of Tambo Viejo, an Inka provincial center where excavations have uncovered tasseled sacrificial llamas and brightly adorned guinea pigs. But save for a few seeds and some stored leaves, evidence of how the Inka used one of their most sacred plants in rituals remained elusive. Now, archaeologists have discovered coca leaves still stuck in the wool of some sacrificed llamas. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Brazilians began casting their votes on Sunday in a closely watch presidential election pitting incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. item.description: Brazilians began casting their votes on Sunday in a closely watch presidential election pitting incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Nearly 160 million voters will also pick lawmakers, senators and governors in an election that will determine whether Latin America's biggest nation follows a regional swing to the right championed by US President Donald Trump. France 24 correspondent Jan Onoszko tells us the latest from Rio de Janeiro. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Informe desde Río de Janeiro: Brasil vota con baja probabilidad de definir en primera vuelta
item.description: Brasil inició este domingo una jornada electoral decisiva. Más de 158 millones de ciudadanos están convocados a las urnas para elegir presidente, vicepresidente, gobernadores, diputados y parte del Senado. Los centros de votación permanecerán abiertos hasta las 17:00, hora de Brasilia. Las encuestas apuntan a una contienda muy ajustada, por lo que la posibilidad de una definición en primera vuelta parece reducida. En 2022, la abstención fue del 20,9 %, es decir, cerca de uno de cada cinco electores no votó. Desde Río de Janeiro, nuestra corresponsal Valeria Saccone nos cuenta más. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: More than 1,200 Colorado students have earned a climate ‘seal’: ‘We’re the ones growing up in this world’
item.description: A statewide initiative pairs climate-focused coursework with community service – and is spreading to other states As a student at a high school not far from Denver’s main airport, Anthony Muñoz wondered whether the jet fuel from airplanes flying above his campus was harming living things. An avid gardener, Muñoz partnered with a local university to create a garden on the campus of his charter school, Vista Academy, filling it with native plants that could detect ground-level ozone pollution. item.title: Lula and Bolsonaro face off in Brazil presidential race
item.description: Twelve candidates are on the ballot, but the presidential race is centred on two rivals: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro. Lula is seeking a fourth and final term, warning that Brazil’s sovereignty is at stake amid pressure from Donald Trump. Bolsonaro, meanwhile, has highlighted his ties to the White House, saying Brazil needs better deals with the US, including over its rare mineral resources. Nick Rushworth has more on the controversial senator. Dr Andrea Aruska de Souza Santos, Director of King's College Brazil Institute in London, shares further insights.
